# SK7010 — Public API without a documentation comment

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

Doc-comment coverage of the publicly visible surface, reported as a metric and — opt-in — as a finding.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Maintainability |
| Default severity | none |
| Scope | Syntax |
| Needs a compilation | no |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 0.8 |

## Why

Comment density is the metric most likely to be gamed and the one most worth having as a *number* rather than as a finding. As an aggregate it says whether a library's public surface is documented; as a per-member warning on a repository that has never documented anything it produces thousands of findings on day one and gets switched off by lunchtime. So it ships disabled — `defaultSeverity: none` — and a repository that wants it turns it on for the paths where it means something, exactly the way doc 08 § SK1000 describes for the hot-path rules. The aggregate is computed either way and appears in the report and in `skala trend`.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
public sealed class Archetype {
    public int Count { get; }
}
```

Write:

```csharp
/// <summary>A set of components stored together.</summary>
public sealed class Archetype {
    /// <summary>How many entities the archetype holds.</summary>
    public int Count { get; }
}
```

## When it does not fire

Disabled by default, so it produces nothing until a repository asks for it. When enabled it counts only members that are publicly visible through their whole containing chain, ignores accessors, explicit interface implementations, operators, finalizers, compiler-generated members, `record` positional members and anything in generated code, and treats an `<inheritdoc/>` as documentation.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK7010.severity (`none` by default; set it per path to enable)`
